scope: runtime, component/model/plugin/service contracts; persistent-data and security domains require companion research

contracts.story: As a host, I initialize and retire one agent runtime so plugins see one stable identity and shared resources close only after dependent work settles.
rules: Require explicit adapter and perform adapter readiness/initialization before agent persistence and room bootstrap.
Release initPromise on initialization failure, preserve failure, and suppress service starts after failed initialization.
Publish stop ownership before synchronous prepareStop reentrancy. Close queue admission and abort turns before first drain.
Strict stop requires generation-stable empty room queue, post-delivery tracker, and retirement; retained failures reject later strict calls.
close stops adapter scheduler, drains before-close work, and coordinates adapter close through existing ownership.
scenarios: strict stop after earlier bounded stop

contracts.story: As a plugin author, I register, reconfigure and unload declared contributions with identity-safe cleanup.
rules: Concurrent same-name registrations share the same pending result.
Initialize hook precedes declared contribution registration; configurations stringify non-null primitives.
Ownership tracks exact references and includes async service start contributions.
Rollback preserves original failure and reports cleanup failure.
Plugin-boundary action/provider/evaluator overrides remain first-wins; direct host override can replace.
Unload only owned contributions; successor connector ownership survives predecessor unload. Adapter-owning plugin requires runtime reload.
Concurrent unload shares one teardown; service stop shared across unload and runtime stop.
scenarios: old connector owner unloads after replacement

contracts.story: As a plugin, I acquire a typed service without duplicate starts and observe honest readiness.
rules: Register all sibling implementations before eager startup.
Deduplicate per service class; parallel siblings retain declared order. getService returns first available and getServicesByType returns all.
No instance is published after stop request; late instance gets its single stop operation.
SERVICE_STARTED runs after publication so observers use synchronous lookup; observer failure is reported without invalidating service.
Eager startup delays are 2000,5000,10000 ms and cease on stop.
All-implementation failure carries SERVICE_START_FAILED and aggregate cause.

contracts.story: As a host, I register extension components with deterministic collision rules.
state: registry of name to component reference
rules: Same reference registration is idempotent.
Same-name nonoverride retains first and warns.
Direct declared override replaces exact slot while plugin registration neutralizes it.
Unregister returns a truthful existence result.

contracts.story: As an agent, I execute an action only through the common authorization and settlement boundary.
rules: Private, disclosure, product allowlist, request restriction, operator policy and declared role/context checks run consistently across exposure and execution.
Operator role policy replaces declared gates after nonoverridable private/disclosure/product/request gates.
Raw operation restriction is effect-free and negative-only.
No validator or handler may turn a rejected gate into authorization.
Mode actions validate concurrently then use stable priority/name order; DURING modes run concurrently while other modes run sequentially.
Every handler must return plain ActionResult with explicit success boolean; trusted executor overwrites action identity.
Separate handler failure from callback delivery failure to avoid replaying committed mutations.

contracts.story: As a caller, I receive mutation claims only when exact text binds to validated durable receipts.
rules: Receipts distinguish applied, preview, noop, failed and rolled_back states with resource and idempotency evidence.
Mutating action callbacks buffer until settlement.
Claimed user-facing receipt IDs resolve only to validated result receipts.
Canonical user-facing text must match callback text, and replayed noop has original commitment provenance.
Visible delivered outcome cannot upgrade preview, failed or rolled-back evidence to applied.

contracts.story: As a turn, I compose complete authorized context while sharing equivalent provider work.
rules: Default providers exclude private/dynamic unless explicitly requested. onlyInclude limits hook expansion.
Providers are ordered by position then name; result selection and merge remain stable under parallel completion.
Cache keys include room and attested audience. Owner-private material is reauthorized and excluded from shared mixed state cache.
Refresh only named and uncached providers; source input or selection change invalidates prior state.
Cancellation ends caller waiting but shared work ownership must remain correct for other waiters; stop aborts all keyed and one-off executions.
Provider failures remain explicit in execution records; context bytes and provenance remain complete.

contracts.story: As a caller, I invoke registered model capabilities with typed failures, cancellation and truthful provider attribution.
rules: Model type fallback uses existing canonical chain and priority/registration order. Explicit provider and ELIZA_BRAIN_PROVIDER are strict pins.
Capability disabled differs from no provider; typed error reason preserves distinction.
Embedding model is pinned to boot-verified provider/vector-space identity and never silently fails over.
Clone and freeze complete admitted request; admit real final wire budget including tools/schema and reject overflow explicitly.
Never remove prompt content to satisfy a limit.
Failover only eligible failures before observable output and remaining retry budget; abort and malformed output remain failures.
Attribution records actual provider/model/attempt and usage, preserving unknown as unknown.

contracts.story: As a host, I extend one structured response schema while preserving source and routing authority.
rules: All fields remain schema-required and inactive fields use defined defaults.
Parse all active field values before priority-ordered handlers; sibling parsed values are read-only.
Preemption aborts later work and selects ack-and-stop, ignore or direct-reply.
Evaluator deterministic calls require exact declared allowed action names.
Only trusted evaluator sources can extend complete canonical context; model output cannot author authority or invalidation ownership.
Patch invalidation protects core source/evidence/routing fields.

contracts.story: As a memory processor, I reconcile complete source-bound evidence and commit progress atomically.
rules: Incremental opt-in requires replay-safe processors.
Background inference releases room ownership then revalidates source/prompt under new lease before effects.
Changed and removed messages carry exact source revisions; incomplete prior evidence effects retire before regeneration.
Complete room transcript/shared blocks are rendered once without replacing information.

contracts.story: As a caller, I cancel waiting or active work without prematurely releasing room ownership.
rules: One active room owner; unrelated rooms proceed independently.
Queue admission is bounded with typed saturation errors.
Queued cancellation removes waiter; acquired lease lasts through durable outcome settlement.
In-turn abortTurn excludes its own caller while shutdown abortAllTurns includes all.
CloseAdmissions refuses new work and quiesce waits original owners.

contracts.story: As a plugin, I intercept supported phases with deterministic ordering and explicit failures.
rules: IDs and ownership determine replacement and cleanup.
Per-phase list invalidated on registration changes; position controls order and schedule controls serial/concurrent execution.
Ordinary hook failures are reported and isolated; local admission unavailability propagates before dispatch.
Outgoing sanitize and guarded stream admission run after transformations.

contracts.story: As a host, I configure one agent without reviving revoked credentials.
rules: Lookup order character secrets, direct settings, extra settings, nested secrets, character env, runtime settings; preserve boolean and number.
setSetting null deletes both live and legacy copied slots so fallback cannot resurrect revoked credentials.
String decryption uses configured salt; production forbids historical public salt.
Explicit host env fallbacks remain scoped and documented.

contracts.story: As a memory consumer, I read and write vectors in one verified coordinate space.
rules: Boot probe establishes width and concrete provider/model identity.
Store identity changes require explicit acceptance/re-embedding policy.
Embedding queue results cannot mix dimensions or silent provider failover.
Existing empty or legacy store identity is explicitly reconciled.

surfaces.name: PipelineHookPhase
surfaces.declaration:
export type PipelineHookPhase =
	| "incoming_before_compose"
	/**
	 * Inside `composeState`, after the runtime selects the provider NAMES for the
	 * turn (default selection + context routing, or an explicit include-list) but
	 * before any provider's `get()` runs. Hooks reassign `providers.current` to
	 * filter, extend, or reorder the set — letting a host app shape context per
	 * message intent (e.g. drop heavy wallet/ledger providers on a greeting, add
	 * `CRYPTO_SWAP` when transaction keywords appear). Opt-in: zero cost and
	 * identical behavior when no hook is registered. Mutator phase (serial,
	 * `mutatesPrimary`), so multiple hooks compose in `position` order.
	 *
	 * Contract: reassign `providers.current` to a `string[]`; a non-array value is
	 * ignored and the pre-hook selection is kept (a thrown hook is swallowed and
	 * continues, like every phase). Keep selection **deterministic for a given
	 * message** — `composeState` caches by `message.id`. The hook also fires for
	 * curated/internal calls (`onlyInclude === true`, e.g. response composition);
	 * those pass an exact list the runtime depends on, so gate on `onlyInclude` and
	 * no-op unless you mean to override them.
	 */
	| "compose_state_providers"
	| "pre_should_respond"
	/**
	 * Overlaps the should-respond phase (heuristics + optional classifier). **All** hooks for this
	 * phase run concurrently in one `Promise.all` — `position`, `schedule`, and `mutatesPrimary`
	 * do not create serial ordering or mutator-first buckets (unlike other phases). Prefer
	 * `pre_should_respond` for ordered mutators / readers.
	 */
	| "parallel_with_should_respond"
	| "outgoing_before_deliver"
	/** Immediately before the registered model `handler` runs (`AgentRuntime.useModel`). */
	| "pre_model"
	/** After the model handler returns (including stream consumption). Replace output via `result.current`. */
	| "post_model"
	/**
	 * After `createMemory` successfully wrote to the adapter; `memory.id` is the persisted id.
	 * Runs for every table (e.g. `messages`, `knowledge`); filter on `tableName` when needed.
	 * Set `memory.content.metadata.skipAfterMemoryPersistedHooks === true` to skip (rare).
	 */
	| "after_memory_persisted"
	/**
	 * Per stream delta: raw provider tokens from `useModel`'s `textStream` loop (`source: "use_model"`),
	 * plus **async** `onStreamChunk` boundaries (`message_service`, …).
	 * On Node, `message_service` is skipped while delivering the same chunk from `useModel`
	 * (see `getModelStreamChunkDeliveryDepth` in `streaming-context.ts`) to avoid duplicate hooks.
	 * High frequency: default `applyPipelineHooks` disables per-hook telemetry for this phase.
	 */
	| "model_stream_chunk"
	/**
	 * After a streaming leg ends: `useModel` when `textStream` is exhausted (before `post_model`),
	 * or `onStreamEnd` in action streaming context.
	 * Best-effort `text` when the caller tracks accumulated stream text.
	 */
	| "model_stream_end";

SchemaRow
surfaces.declaration:
export type SchemaRow = SchemaValueSpec & {
	/** Field name in structured JSON output */
	field: string;
	/**
	 * Control per-field validation codes for streaming (levels 0-1 only).
	 *
	 * WHY: Validation codes are UUID snippets that surround each field. If the LLM
	 * outputs the same code before and after a field, we know the context window
	 * wasn't truncated mid-field. This trades off token usage for reliability.
	 *
	 * Behavior by level:
	 * - Level 0 (Trusted): default false. Set to true to opt-in to per-field codes.
	 * - Level 1 (Progressive): default true. Set to false to opt-out of codes.
	 * - Levels 2-3: ignored for per-field wrapping. Those levels can use optional
	 * checkpoint codes instead.
	 *
	 * Note: Only top-level schema rows use this today. Nested `properties` are still
	 * validated structurally, but they do not get their own streaming/validation wires.
	 */
	validateField?: boolean;
	/**
	 * Control whether this field's content is streamed to the consumer.
	 *
	 * WHY: Not all fields should be shown to users in real-time:
	 * - 'thought': Internal reasoning - might be verbose or confusing to show
	 * - 'actions': System field for action routing - not user-visible
	 * - 'text': The actual response - should definitely stream
	 *
	 * Default: true for 'text' field, false for others.
	 *
	 * Note: Only top-level schema rows are considered for streaming. Nested object/array
	 * members still flow through parsing/validation, but are not streamed independently.
	 */
	streamField?: boolean;
};
